label: ECDLP, prime-field curves
problem: Discrete logarithm in a prime-order subgroup of an elliptic curve over a prime field, using generic collision attacks and the universally available negation map.

reference.label: P-256-sized group
reference.why: A fixed illustrative group-order size. The plotted birthday-model index is not a complete concrete security estimate for every 256-bit curve.

notes: Selected classical collision-cost models, not an exhaustive attack history. The constant-factor negation saving changes the modeled cost by 0.5 bits while the square-root exponent stays unchanged. Additional automorphisms, weak curve families, parallel hardware and implementation costs require separate analyses. The group-order parameter must not be confused with field size: for example, Curve25519 has a roughly 252-bit prime-order subgroup.
assumptions: An idealized random walk and birthday-collision calculation give k sqrt(r) for subgroup order r. Per-step costs, cycle handling, coordination and memory are omitted. Both entries use the same model; a flat selected envelope is not evidence that all cryptanalysis stopped.

milestones.name: Pollard rho: idealized birthday model
milestones.ref: Monte Carlo methods for index computation (mod p), Mathematics of Computation 32 (1978), 918–924
milestones.assumptions: Random-mapping heuristic; k = sqrt(pi/2) counts idealized steps to a useful collision, not the complete cost of a particular cycle-detection implementation. The 1978 generic-group method predates elliptic-curve cryptography.
milestones.notes: Inherited baseline when the displayed curve timeline begins in 1985.

milestones.name: Negation-map collision model
milestones.authors: Michael J. Wiener; Robert J. Zuccherato
milestones.ref: Faster Attacks on Elliptic Curve Cryptosystems, SAC 1998, LNCS 1556 (1999), 190–200
milestones.assumptions: Identifying a point with its negative halves the idealized collision search space. Efficient handling of fruitless cycles and negligible negation overhead are assumed.
milestones.notes: The source reports a sqrt(2) speedup for arbitrary curves. This is a constant-factor modeled-cost improvement, not an exponent improvement. Dated to SAC 1998, rather than the 1999 proceedings year.
